original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Exact minimum paid-call cost for every diagonal target diag([g],[h]) with (g,h) in S3 squared, using two arbitrary dirty scalar registers, the transposition labels x=(12), y=(23), and rank-one idempotent factors I+([s]+[1])N.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue permits a specified nonabelian family. The first bounded inverse-3-cycle pair had no saving; one evidence-driven pivot expanded the same S3/two-register model to all 36 target pairs, to determine whether no-sharing was target-specific. No further expansion was made.
bottleneck_link: This screens whether a changed finite nonabelian bit alphabet permits paid-call sharing across two targets. The group has no physical map to the selected rational-frame supplier, so the result is a scoped alternative-model bound and cannot change the selected recursive profile.
stop_rule: Exhaust the complete radius-five ball over the twelve paid generators. For each of the 36 target pairs, compare its shortest transposition-word direct construction with the exact ball distance. Since every separate bill is at most six, radius five covers every possible strict saving. Stop at two registers, S3, the two labels, and all diagonal target pairs.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json records the complete radius-five layers [1,12,80,466,2345,10760] (13,664 distinct products), exact minima for all 36 pairs, the equal direct-call histogram, 1,885 raw-word literal replays, 13,664 canonical-path formal replays, and 108 omitted-factor controls.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No predecessor code was imported.

open_questions.question: Does a third arbitrary dirty register permit any shared-call saving for an S3 target triple, for example diag([xyx],[xyx],1) with the same paid transpositions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This would test whether the exact two-register no-sharing result depends on role count and could expose a new multi-target mechanism.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate the 56 rank-one-idempotent generators for three registers and measure exact radius-four state growth for the fixed target before searching deeper.
open_questions.blocked_by: The generator count and state ball grow quickly; the two-register result supplies no lower bound for the expanded role model.

source_baseline: PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY; complex primitive binds; selected kappa unchanged.
